title: Why are sunsets orange? (It's not the sun)

hook.narration: The sun doesn't turn orange. Your sky just runs out of blue.

visual.pose: skygawk (shield-eyes at a giant low sun)
visual.prop: low sun + orange horizon + kinetic title

fact_sources: premise restatement — Rayleigh path-length physics, no numbers on screen

scenes.narration: Sunlight looks white — but it's carrying every color at once.

visual.prop: white beam → rainbow fan through air wedge

fact_sources: white light = superposition of the visible spectrum (textbook; fan is schematic)

scenes.narration: Air is a sieve: molecules fling blue sideways about six times harder than red.

visual.prop: molecule + blue ricochet vs red drift, 'BLUE ≈ 6×' pop

fact_sources: Rayleigh scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴ (Wikipedia, Lord Rayleigh); (700/450)⁴ = 5.86 ≈ 'about six' — computed 2026-11-08

scenes.narration: At noon, your beam crosses one patch of air. At sunset? Thirty-eight.
fact_sources: Air mass 1 at zenith → ≈38 at horizon (Kasten & Young 1989, via Wikipedia 'Air mass (astronomy)')

scenes.narration: Thirty-eight times the air, and every step bleeds more blue away. What survives the whole trip is orange.

visual.pose: amazed (lit orange by the arriving beam)
visual.prop: long grazing beam in 4 segments white→orange, blue photons peeling off

fact_sources: same Rayleigh law + airmass 38; beam color progression schematic (no numeric claim)

scenes.narration: The blue that got thrown out? It never dies — it becomes the rest of your sky.

visual.prop: photons raining up into a glowing blue dome over the orange beam

fact_sources: scattered blue light IS the sky's blue (same Rayleigh mechanism; sky opposite the sun stays blue at sunset)

scenes.narration: Same sun. Same air. Only the angle changed.

visual.prop: three stamps: SAME SUN / SAME AIR / ONLY THE ANGLE

scenes.narration: On Mars, dust flips the trick — blue sunsets. Go watch yours tonight.

visual.prop: butterscotch Mars sky + BLUE halo sun → back to our hill

fact_sources: NASA JPL 'Curiosity Rover Views Serene Sundown on Mars' (2015-05-08): dust forward-scatters blue, blue glow stays near the sun
